title: Secrets of Religion
author: Unknown
description: Secrets of Religion (Studies of the Past) by the pseudonymous 'Vindex Veri', published in Manchester by 'The Two Worlds' Publishing Co. in 1901, the press of the leading British Spiritualist newspaper. Taking as its motto Confucius's 'We must study the past to understand the present', the book is a freethinking Spiritualist critique of orthodox Christianity through comparative religion. Over many chapters it traces Christian doctrines, festivals and stories back to older solar and astral myths, mystery religions and the faiths of Egypt, India, Persia and Babylon, arguing that the churches have obscured a universal natural religion. It reflects the comparative mythology and anticlerical currents of late Victorian Spiritualism and is of interest for the history of 'Christ myth' and pagan-origins arguments.
